standard_prerequisites: Structure theorem for finite abelian groups: a finite abelian group decomposes as Z/e_1Z + ... + Z/e_rZ with 1 < e_1 | e_2 | ... | e_r

Divisor sum identity: the sum of d over the divisors d of n equals n; for e_1 dividing each e_i, the e_1-torsion of the factor Z/e_iZ has exactly e_1 elements, so the e_1-torsion of the direct sum has e_1^r elements
core_obligations: Every element of A has order d for some divisor d of n, and elements of exact order d are among the d-torsion, which has at most d elements; hence |A| <= sum over d | n of d = n, so A is finite
Write A = Z/e_1Z + ... + Z/e_rZ by the structure theorem; the e_1-torsion then has e_1^r elements, but the hypothesis bounds it by e_1, so r = 1
With r = 1 the group is cyclic, and its order equals the exponent, which divides n
proof_roadmap: Bound the group order by divisor counting
Kill the rank of the decomposition through the e_1-torsion count
